study_type_evidence.quote: Dosing was by intravenous bolus in all studies, routinely at weekly intervals (qw)
Plasma protein binding and plasma stability were assessed in plasma from CD1 mouse, Sprague–Dawley rat, cynomolgus monkey and human.
Binding affinities were determined using a fluorescence polarization assay during the early-screening phase and later by surface plasmon resonance (SPR)

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: BALB/c nude or CB17-SCID (CDX/PDX at WuXi AppTec); 6- to 8-week-old female athymic Nude-Foxn1nu (PDX at Champions Oncology)
in_vivo_species.quote: Cell-derived xenograft (CDX) studies were conducted in BALB/c nude, or CB17-SCID mice inoculated with approximately 107 cells in the right flank.

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: not reported in the toxicology section; Sprague-Dawley named for the in vitro matrices
in_vivo_species.quote: Repeat dose studies with BT8009 were performed in rat (1, 3, and 5 mg/kg/occasion)

ex_vivo_detail: Plasma protein binding and plasma stability of BT8009 were assessed in plasma taken from CD1 mouse, Sprague-Dawley rat and cynomolgus monkey (human plasma also used). Stability was additionally assessed in hepatocytes and microsomes from the same species. In vitro stability in mouse plasma was substantially lower than in the other species, attributed to Ces1c. Studies conducted at WuXi AppTec.
in_vitro_detail: SPR and fluorescence polarization binding to Nectin-4 extracellular domain from human and toxicology species and to Nectin/Nectin-like family members; high-content imaging of BT8009, Nectin-4 ADC, BCY8781 and MMAE binding to live MDA-MB-468 cells at 4 °C; Retrogenix screen of BCY9565 against 5,528 human plasma membrane and secreted proteins in HEK293 cells; electrophysiological patch-clamp on hERG, hNav1.5 and Kv1.5; Nectin-4 expression by flow cytometry with Quantibrite beads; hepatocyte and microsome intrinsic clearance.

agents.name: BT8009
agents.sequence_source: body describes a 26 amino acid linear peptide (binder plus sarcosine decamer spacer) cyclized with TATA, but prints no amino acid sequence; structures are relegated to Supplementary Chemical Structures
agents.chemical_identifier: Bicycle Toxin Conjugate, molecular mass 4171 (~4.2 kDa); Nectin-4-binding bicyclic peptide BCY8126; biotinylated binder BCY9565; toxin-linker glutaric acid-valine-citrulline-PABC-MMAE; peptide:toxin ratio 1:1
agents.group_n: n = 3 per timepoint (PK); n = 3-5 (efficacy studies); n = 3-16 (head-to-head ADC studies)
agents.group_n_quote: Error bars indicate SD of n = 3 per timepoint.
agents.dose: mouse: 1-3 mg/kg qw (3 mg/kg standard), also 5 mg/kg; biw and q2w regimens also used. Rat: 1, 3, 5 mg/kg/occasion. NHP: 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 mg/kg/occasion
agents.route: intravenous bolus (mouse xenograft studies); short 15-minute intravenous infusion once weekly for 5 doses (rat and NHP toxicology)
agents.dose_route_quote: Dosing was by intravenous bolus in all studies, routinely at weekly intervals (qw)
agents.half_life: 0.9 hours (rat); 1.7 hours (non-human primate). Mouse terminal half-life is not given numerically in the body
agents.half_life_matrix: rat plasma and non-human primate plasma
agents.cmax: not reported numerically (body states only that 'high systemic Cmax values can be attained')
agents.pk_quote: BT8009 t1/2 rat = 0.9 hours; t1/2 NHP = 1.7 hours

agents.name: MMAE (mono-methylauristatin E)
agents.chemical_identifier: mono-methylauristatin E; cell-permeant antimitotic toxin payload of BT8009 and of enfortumab vedotin
agents.group_n: n = 4-8 (high content imaging); n = 3 per timepoint (tumour/plasma PK)
agents.group_n_quote: High content imaging showing anti-MMAE mAb staining after incubation of MDA-MB-468 cells with test agent (each at 1 μmol/L) n = 4–8
agents.dose: 1 μmol/L in the cell binding assay; not administered alone in vivo
agents.route: in vitro only as an unconjugated agent; measured as a circulating and tumour analyte after BT8009 dosing
agents.cmax: not reported numerically; peak tumour concentrations of total MMAE attained within 2-4 hours
agents.pk_quote: After administration of BT8009 peak tumor concentrations of total MMAE were rapidly attained within 2–4 hours

agents.name: BCY8781 (non-binding BTC homologue)
agents.sequence_source: body states only that two key-binding residues of BCY8126 were substituted (L-Trp replaced with D-Trp); no sequence is printed
agents.chemical_identifier: BCY8781; comparable physicochemical properties to BT8009 but lacking affinity for Nectin-4
agents.group_n_quote: Tumor volumes are shown as mean ± standard error of the mean (n = 3–5)
agents.dose: equivalent doses to BT8009 (specific mg/kg values not stated in the body)
agents.dose_route_quote: In the LU-01–0412 PDX model, BT8009 consistently showed greater tumor regression than the non-binding homologue BCY8781 at equivalent doses.

agents.name: BCY8234 (MMAE-free analogue of BT8009)
agents.group_n_quote: Tumor volumes are shown as mean ± standard error of the mean (n = 3–5)
agents.dose: 130-fold excess relative to BT8009 (absolute mg/kg not stated)
agents.route: co-administered with BT8009 (intravenous bolus per the general dosing statement)
agents.dose_route_quote: BT8009 was co-administered with a 130-fold excess of BCY8234, an MMAE-free analogue of BT8009.

agents.name: Nectin-4 ADC (in-house enfortumab vedotin analog)
agents.chemical_identifier: molecular weight 152 kDa, DAR of 3.98; antibody from GenScript USA, ADC generated at WuXi Biologics; valine-citrulline-MMAE linker-payload
agents.group_n_quote: Tumor volumes are shown as mean ± standard error of the mean (n = 3–16)
agents.dose: 5 mg/kg on D0 and D7, increased to 10 mg/kg on D14; literature-based EV doses of 10 or 4 mg/kg single dose, or 3 mg/kg every 4 days
agents.dose_route_quote: ADC was dosed at 5 mg/kg on D0 and D7, then increased to 10 mg/kg on D14.
agents.half_life: not reported for the in-house ADC; the body cites literature values for enfortumab vedotin of t1/2 rat = 1-1.3 days and t1/2 NHP = 0.7-1.7 days
agents.half_life_matrix: rat and non-human primate plasma (literature values for enfortumab vedotin)
agents.pk_quote: EV t1/2 rat = 1–1.3 days; t1/2 NHP = 0.7–1.7 days; EV multi-disciplinary review and evaluation

agents.name: BCY8126 (Nectin-4-binding bicyclic peptide)
agents.chemical_identifier: BCY8126; binding peptide incorporated into BT8009
agents.dose: not reported (in vitro only: SPR and cardiac ion channel patch clamp)
agents.dose_route_quote: in a functional cardiac ion assay the Bicycle binder (BCY8126) had no activity on the three tested ion channels (hERG, hNav1.5 and Kv1.5)

agents.name: BCY9565 (biotinylated Bicycle binder)
agents.chemical_identifier: BCY9565; biotinylated form of the Bicycle binder present in BT8009
agents.dose: not reported (Retrogenix screen against 5,528 human membrane and secreted proteins)
agents.dose_route_quote: Selectivity of the biotinylated Bicycle binder (BCY9565) present in BT8009 was assessed in a Retrogenix assay against 5,528 human full-length human plasma membrane proteins

agents.name: Vehicle
agents.group_n_quote: Tumor volumes are shown as mean ± standard error of the mean (n = 3–5)
agents.dose_route_quote: All studies included a vehicle-treated control.

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: PK profile of BT8009 and MMAE in three mouse xenograft models. MMAE is rapidly cleared from plasma but retained in tumor substantially longer.
concentration_time_figure.note: Plasma, tumour and (in two models) muscle concentrations of BT8009 and MMAE vs time over 24-72 h in NCI-H292, MDA-MB-468 and NCI-H322 CDX models. Supplementary Fig. S1 (not in body text) is cited for circulating parent and MMAE levels and Supplementary Table S3 for the PK parameters.

bioanalytical_quote: BT8009 and MMAE levels were quantified in plasma and tumor samples following analyte extraction and bioanalysis using LC/MS-MS assays.
notes: No mouse half-life value appears anywhere in the body; the only numeric terminal half-lives given are rat (0.9 h) and NHP (1.7 h), both in the Discussion. Mouse Vdss is stated as 0.25 L/kg (vs 0.08 L/kg for EV). The full mouse/rat/NHP PK parameter table is in Supplementary Table S3 and is not reproduced in the body. Cmax is discussed only qualitatively ('high Cmax'), with no number. The Discussion reports interim Phase 1 clinical results (50% confirmed overall response rate in eight urothelial cancer patients dosed at 5.0 mg/m2 weekly), but that trial is not part of the work described in this paper, so 'clinical' is not listed as a study type. A second Nectin-4 ADC, N41mab-vcMMAE, is cited from the literature only and was not tested here. Amino acid sequences and structures for all Bicycle agents are in Supplementary Chemical Structures, not the body; the sequence in the PEPLIFE2 header is database metadata and was not used. The MTD was 5 mg/kg in rat and 1.5 mg/kg in NHP.
